relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: Marianne Winder began studying German as an external student at the University of London. On gaining her honours degree in 1948

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: she obtained a post as Tutorial Assistant in the Department of German at the University of Nottingham.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: At Nottingham she completed a Master's thesis on the etymology of High Middle German words

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.object: Institute of Germanic Studies at the University of London
relations.evidence: In 1953 Winder was appointed Assistant Librarian at the Institute of Germanic Studies at the University of London

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: graduated in 1963 with a degree in Librarianship from University College London.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.object: Wellcome Library at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine
relations.evidence: At this time she accepted the position of Assistant Librarian in the Wellcome Library at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine where she was to remain for the rest of her career.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: She collaborated with Dr. Walter Pagel, a pathologist and medical historian, and co-authored with him several articles

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: Christmas Humphreys who, according to her, had had the most beneficial influence on her life.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: succeeded Mrs Carlo Robins as editor-in-chief from 1961 to 1965

relations.subject: Muriel Daw
relations.evidence: from 1961 to 1965, when she was succeeded by Muriel Daw.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.object: School of Oriental and African Studies
relations.evidence: Winder was also interested in the language and culture of Tibet and took lessons in Tibetan at the School of Oriental and African Studies.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.object: Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine
relations.role: Curator of Oriental Manuscripts and Prints
relations.evidence: When the position of Curator of Oriental Manuscripts and Prints was created at the Wellcome Institute in 1970 she gained it.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: At the same time she began a collaboration with Rechung Rinpoché Jampal Kunzang which led to the publication in 1973 of Tibetan Medicine: Illustrated in Original Texts

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.evidence: Always willing to learn, the new Curator attended all the classes of the English Tibetologist David Snellgrove.

relations.subject: Marianne Winder
relations.object: Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine
relations.evidence: Upon her retirement from the Wellcome Institute in 1978 Winder was appointed Consultant in Tibetan Medicine at the Institute

relations.subject: Nigel Allan
relations.evidence: Her successor at the Wellcome Institute was Nigel Allan.
